headline: High risk: n8n can read/write shared files and run commands, so pairing with kotaemon can leak sensitive documents and amplify prompt-injection or workflow errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: kotaemon ingests documents, PDFs, HTML, MHTML, XLSX, DOC/DOCX and chat transcripts, while n8n can read/write the server filesystem and orchestrate tools as workflow nodes. If n8n passes kotaemon-generated content into workflows, attacker-controlled document text can be treated as instructions. The shared-file and workflow bridge makes injection plausible in default setups.
conditions: IF n8n workflows ingest kotaemon outputs without provenance checks, prompt injection is reachable.
IF shared files are used as the handoff channel, attacker-authored document text can steer downstream actions.
mitigations: Add a provenance tag to every kotaemon output before n8n consumes it.
Restrict n8n workflows to allowlisted input folders only.
Insert a human review step before any action-taking node.
Use separate service accounts and directories for the two systems.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-stripping at the workflow boundary.

B_data_leakage.rationale: kotaemon explicitly handles documents, PDFs, chat transcripts, and API keys, and n8n can read the server filesystem plus broad integration-node APIs. That creates a direct path for sensitive files or secrets from kotaemon's workspace into n8n workflows and then to external services. The blast radius includes exfiltration of API keys and customer documents.
conditions: IF n8n workflows can access kotaemon's ./ktem_app_data or exported documents, leakage is possible.
IF any n8n integration node forwards those files to a third-party API, exfiltration occurs.
mitigations: Place kotaemon and n8n on separate volumes with no shared write access.
Rotate any API keys already stored in kotaemon.
Disable or restrict n8n nodes that send files off-box.
Audit the first 5 workflows for file-read and upload steps.
requires-engineering: enforce per-workflow data-loss-prevention rules.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress, and n8n can write the filesystem while kotaemon stores app data locally and supports multiple instances. If they share a directory or connected system, concurrent writes can corrupt artifacts or overwrite outputs. Because n8n also runs shell commands, the conflict can extend beyond files into side effects on the host.
conditions: IF both agents point at the same host directory, write conflicts are reachable.
IF n8n workflows mutate files that kotaemon also reads, race conditions can corrupt state.
mitigations: Give each agent its own filesystem root.
Disable n8n file-write steps for shared paths.
Run both under separate OS users.
Check for overlapping cron/workflow schedules.
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared mutable resource.

D_cascading_error.rationale: kotaemon produces retrieved answers and citations, and n8n's AI Agent node can chain tool calls from workflow nodes. If n8n treats kotaemon output as authoritative, a mistaken or injected answer can cascade into emails, tickets, or other automated actions. The interaction is plausible but not guaranteed because it depends on workflow design.
conditions: IF n8n uses kotaemon output as a decision input without verification, errors can cascade.
IF a workflow node sends external messages based on that output, downstream harm increases.
mitigations: Add a verification step before any action node.
Require citations or source links for kotaemon-derived claims.
Limit AI Agent workflows to read-only mode initially.
Review the first 3 automations that consume kotaemon output.
requires-engineering: implement confidence thresholds before execution.

E_compliance.rationale: kotaemon handles customer-support documents, chat transcripts, and API keys, while n8n processes whatever the workflow touches and can send data through many integrations. That creates a compliance mismatch risk if regulated or sensitive data is routed into workflows with different retention, logging, or residency settings. The profiles do not prove a specific residency breach, so medium is the higher justified level.
conditions: IF regulated customer-support data enters an n8n workflow with different retention settings, compliance drift occurs.
IF workflow logs retain API keys or transcripts longer than kotaemon's handling policy, the mismatch is material.
mitigations: Map the data classes each workflow touches.
Shorten retention on workflows handling transcripts or keys.
Disable verbose execution logs for sensitive flows.
Confirm residency for every external integration.
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion policies across both systems.
